headline: Coates beats De Graaf in a decider for his first Grand Slam win
standfirst: Henry Coates kept Group L alive a day after missing two match darts against Michael van Gerwen.
body: Henry Coates recorded his first Grand Slam of Darts win on Sunday night, beating Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4 in a deciding leg to keep Group L firmly in the balance.

The 20-year-old debutant had lost his opening match to Michael van Gerwen by the same score on Saturday. He had two match darts in that game, but missed both and the Dutchman checked 56 to win. Twenty-four hours later, Coates took the decider he had just missed out on.

Speaking at his press conference, Coates described the experience as "some of the best memories I've had so far", according to Dartsnews. He said Van Gerwen had told him on stage that he was proud of the way he played and had enjoyed the match, and described that as inspirational coming from one of the sport's greats.

His season has moved quickly. Coates said his original aim was only to stay high enough in the Challenge Tour rankings to keep earning ProTour starts, and that a Players Championship title and a Grand Slam debut were a bonus. He put his composure down to years of junior darts through the JDC.
He also named Martin Adams and Terry Jenkins among his early favourites, recalling that he repeatedly watched Adams' 2010 BDO World Championship final win over Dave Chisnall after school.
Coates' qualification hopes now depend on the final group game.
